text:
The purchaser is likely to prevail because the recorded easement was appurtenant to the woman’s house and passed with the property to the man and then to the purchaser, despite the man’s temporary common ownership. The easement was not extinguished by merger because the man never took actual possession of the house and there was no clear intent to merge the estates. Therefore, the purchaser holds a valid easement and the man cannot barricade the path.

CONFIDENCE: 90
